item.title: #3585886: Outdated _method requirement in CsrfRequestHeaderAccessCheck::applies()
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 5 files, +67/−32 · php +57/−30 · yml +10/−2
  • Diff: 831ce14
  • Discussion: #3585886 · 5 contributors · 12 comments
  • Followers: 6

Summary

CsrfRequestHeaderAccessCheck, the service that decides which routes need the X-CSRF-Token header check, used an outdated way of detecting which HTTP methods a route allows. It looked for the legacy _method route requirement to decide whether a route was read-only (and could skip the check), but modern routes declare allowed methods with the methods property instead, so that optimization silently never applied to them. This didn't cause a security problem, since the check itself already allows GET, HEAD, OPTIONS and TRACE requests, but it meant the check was being unnecessarily evaluated on read-only routes defined the modern way. The fix drops the outdated, partially broken logic and instead declares the check statically for any route that has the _csrf_request_header_token requirement, regardless of how its methods are declared.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: Drupal\Core\Access\CsrfRequestHeaderAccessCheck now implements Drupal\Core\Routing\Access\AccessInterface instead of AccessCheckInterface; its applies(Route $route) method has been removed.

Technical details

Previously CsrfRequestHeaderAccessCheck implemented AccessCheckInterface, which requires an applies(Route $route) method that Drupal calls dynamically per route to decide whether to attach the checker. That method inspected the deprecated _method route requirement and only skipped attaching the check if all required methods were read-only; routes using the modern methods route property never had _method set, so the method-based skip never kicked in for them.

The fix, following a suggestion from longwood in the thread that the check "doesn't need to be dynamic at all," removes applies() and the _method inspection entirely. CsrfRequestHeaderAccessCheck now implements the plain AccessInterface and is registered in core.services.yml with applies_to: _csrf_request_header_token on its access_check service tag, so Drupal's CheckProvider attaches it statically based purely on the presence of that requirement key. The actual read/write distinction is still enforced at runtime inside access(), which already unconditionally allows GET, HEAD, OPTIONS and TRACE requests before checking for the CSRF token header. A new kernel test, CsrfRequestHeaderAccessCheckTest, asserts the checker is attached to routes declaring _csrf_request_header_token regardless of their declared methods, and not attached when the requirement is absent.

Upgrade

If custom code extends CsrfRequestHeaderAccessCheck or type-hints against AccessCheckInterface specifically for this class, update to the new contract: implement Drupal\Core\Routing\Access\AccessInterface and rely on the applies_to service tag attribute instead of overriding applies(). For example, in a service definition:

access_check.header.csrf:
  class: Drupal\Core\Access\CsrfRequestHeaderAccessCheck
  arguments: ['@session_configuration', '@csrf_token']
  tags:
    - { name: access_check, applies_to: _csrf_request_header_token, needs_incoming_request: TRUE }

Routes that rely on this checker should also prefer the methods route property over the deprecated _method requirement key.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: April 20, 2026
  • Committed: July 28, 2026 (3 months later)

Key contributors

  • prudloff (Insite)
  • sourav_paul (Innoraft)
  • smustgrave (Mobomo)
  • longwave (Full Fat Things)

Collaboration

The initial patch by sourav_paul just added a methods-based check alongside the _method fallback. Months later longwood, while working on the related #3613245, reconsidered the whole approach: rather than patching the method-detection logic, he proposed converting the checker to a static applies_to access check keyed on _csrf_request_header_token, which let the entire applies() method be deleted. catch, who committed the change, noted it was "nice to be able to replace all that code with a one-liner."

item.title: #3588847: Update to Symfony 8.1
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Critical task
  • Version: main
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 25 files, +647/−432 · lock +364/−268 · php +207/−98 · json +66/−66 · txt +10
  • Diff: 169100e
  • Discussion: #3588847 · 4 contributors · 25 comments
  • Followers: 9

Summary

Drupal core's development branch (targeting Drupal 12) updates its bundled Symfony components from the 8.0.x series to 8.1.1, along with a matching PHPUnit bump. There is no behavioral change for end users. The practical impact is for developers who write PHPUnit tests: Symfony 8.1 changed how Request and Response expose their public properties (query, request, server, headers), and the old pattern of mocking these classes and assigning those properties directly, which Drupal core's own test suite used extensively, no longer works reliably. Tests need to construct real Request/Response objects instead. Symfony's validator component also deprecates the old ConstraintValidator::initialize()/::validate() methods in favor of validateInContext().

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Requirements: Drupal core (main, targeting Drupal 12) now requires symfony/* packages ^8.1 instead of ^8.0, and bumps phpunit/phpunit to ^12.5.15.
  • Deprecation: Symfony 8.1 deprecates directly setting public properties like $response->headers or $request->query on Request/Response/CacheableResponse (now property hooks), and deprecates ConstraintValidator::initialize()/::validate() in favor of validateInContext().

Technical details

The diff bumps version constraints in composer.json/core/composer.json (and the corresponding composer.lock) for symfony/console, dependency-injection, event-dispatcher, filesystem, finder, http-foundation, http-kernel, mailer, mime, process, routing, runtime, serializer, validator, and yaml from ^8.0 to ^8.1, plus dev dependencies (phpunit/phpunit to satisfy sebastianbergmann/phpunit#6545, symfony/browser-kit, css-selector, dom-crawler, error-handler, lock, var-dumper).

Two small production fixes were needed for compatibility: ConsoleCompilerPass::process() now calls addTag('console.command') instead of setTags(['console.command' => []]), since symfony/console 8.1 conflicts with symfony/dependency-injection below 8.1 and expects the new tagging API (this also absorbs the fix from #3607060, "ConsoleCompilerPass incompatible with symfony/console ≥ 8.1"). PhpMail::mail() now passes an explicit '' default to $this->request->server->get('SERVER_SOFTWARE', ''), since calling ServerBag::get() without a default is newly deprecated.

The bulk of the remaining diff is test suite fallout: BrowserTestBase, FinishResponseSubscriberTest, NegotiationMiddlewareTest, LoggerChannelTest, PhpMailTest, and RoutePathGenerationTraitTest were rewritten to stop stubbing Request/Response and setting properties like ->query, ->server, ->headers directly on the mock, using real new Request()/new Response() (or new CacheableResponse()) instances instead, since Symfony 8.1 turns those properties into property hooks that reject external writes. BrowserTestBase::getTestMethodCaller() was also adjusted to recognize PHPUnit's new invokeTestMethod() caller frame alongside runTest(). New entries were added to core/.deprecation-ignore.txt and core/.phpstan-baseline.php to suppress the newly surfaced Symfony 8.1 deprecations (tagged-service indexing in dependency injection, the HttpFoundation property-hook writes, and ConstraintValidator::initialize()/validate()) until they can be addressed properly.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: May 6, 2026
  • Committed: July 28, 2026 (2 months later)

Key contributors

  • longwave (Full Fat Things)
  • mstrelan (PreviousNext)
  • godotislate
  • catch (Tag1 Consulting, Inc.)

Collaboration

longwave opened and repeatedly rebased this issue over several months as Symfony 8.1 moved through beta and RC releases, at one point bumping priority to critical "in the hope I can avoid rerolling this yet again." godotislate reviewed and asked whether Symfony really intended for Request/Response objects not to be mockable; longwave explained it was a side effect of Symfony adopting property hooks on those classes (tied to sebastianbergmann/phpunit#6545, which forced the PHPUnit bump), adding that using real Request/Response objects instead of mocks "makes the code cleaner" and that the properties "were never meant to be set from outside anyway." catch, on committing, noted that the phpstan baseline additions are "eventual Symfony 9 blockers" and better addressed early.

item.title: #2951046: Allow parsing and writing PHP class constants and enums in YAML files
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Major task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 39 files, +921/−13 · php +835/−11 · yml +86/−2
  • Diff: 2884bf3
  • Discussion: #2951046 · 29 contributors · 139 comments
  • Followers: 58

Summary

Drupal's YAML parser now understands PHP class constants and enum cases, so configuration, service definitions, and recipe files can reference SomeClass::SOME_CONSTANT or SomeEnum::SomeCase instead of hard-coding literal values that have to be kept in sync by hand. A companion enum config schema type lets module authors declare that a config value must be an instance of a specific PHP enum, with validation enforcing it. To make this safe during module installation and config import, when a module or recipe is being installed its enums and constants are made autoloadable even before the module is fully active, so its own default configuration can reference them. Support is deliberately limited to class-based constants and enums; global constants defined in procedural .module files are not supported.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • Deprecation: Drupal\Core\Config\FileStorageFactory and its getSync() method are deprecated in favor of the config.storage.sync service.
  • New API: YAML (including configuration, services and recipes) can now contain !php/const Some\Class::CONST and !php/enum Some\Enum::Case tags; a new enum config schema type with an enum_class key validates that a config value is an instance of that enum.

Technical details

The core change is small: Drupal\Component\Serialization\YamlSymfony::decode() now passes SymfonyYaml::PARSE_CONSTANT alongside the existing flags, which enables Symfony's !php/const and !php/enum YAML tags. Yaml::encode() (Symfony writer) serializes PHP enums using !php/const, which the parser also accepts back, and !php/enum is additionally supported on decode for compatibility with Symfony's documented syntax and to keep behavior consistent regardless of which YAML backend is in use.

A new Drupal\Core\TypedData\Plugin\DataType\Enum primitive type (schema id enum) plus EnumConstraint/EnumConstraintValidator validate that a decoded value is a \UnitEnum instance of the class named in the schema's enum_class key; Comparator::checkValue() and TypedConfig::castValue() were updated to recognize \UnitEnum values.

The harder problem was config install/import: enums and constants referenced in a module's or recipe's own default configuration are not autoloadable via Composer until the providing module is installed. This is solved with a new Drupal\Core\Config\AutoloadingStorage decorator that temporarily registers a throwaway ClassLoader (PSR-4 mapped to the extension's src directory) around read()/readMultiple() calls. The config.storage.sync service is now produced by a new SyncFactory class, which diffs the core.extension list in the sync storage against the active storage to find newly-appearing modules/themes and wraps the sync FileStorage in AutoloadingStorage for just those extensions. ModuleInstaller::checkConfigurationToInstall() does the same for the module(s) currently being installed. StorageComparer was updated to treat AutoloadingStorage the same as FileStorage for its static-cache optimization. Recipes get analogous handling: parseRecipeContents() in Drupal\Core\Recipe\RecipeData catches the InvalidDataTypeException Symfony throws for an unresolvable Drupal\{extension}\... constant/enum, and if that extension exists on disk but isn't installed yet, registers a temporary classloader for it and retries parsing.

Support for constants defined in procedural .module files was explicitly dropped rather than solved, since it would require preloading .module files before parsing config, a complication the maintainers decided wasn't worth it for a legacy pattern that's being phased out.

Upgrade

Prefer !php/const and !php/enum over literal values in your own config/service YAML, e.g.:

cardinality: !php/const Drupal\Core\Field\FieldStorageDefinitionInterface::CARDINALITY_UNLIMITED
status: !php/enum Drupal\my_module\MyEnum::SomeCase

Declare a matching config schema for enum-typed values:

my_module.settings:
  mapping:
    status:
      type: enum
      enum_class: '\Drupal\my_module\MyEnum'

If your code calls Drupal\Core\Config\FileStorageFactory::getSync() directly, switch to the service instead:

// Before:
$storage = FileStorageFactory::getSync();
// After:
$storage = \Drupal::service('config.storage.sync');

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: March 8, 2018
  • Committed: July 27, 2026 (8 years and 2 commits later)

Key contributors

  • marcoscano (MD Systems GmbH)
  • dawehner (Chapter Three (acquired by Kanopi Studios))
  • amateescu
  • alexpott (Acro Commerce)
  • andypost (Skilld)
  • neclimdul (APQC)
  • gapple
  • narendrar (Acquia)
  • mikelutz (Four Kitchens)
  • longwave (Full Fat Things)
  • phenaproxima (Acquia)
  • mondrake
  • eduardo morales alberti (Metadrop)
  • wim leers (Acquia)
  • dcam
  • borisson_ (Calibrate)
  • bircher (Nuvole)
  • catch (Third and Grove)
  • kristiaanvandeneynde (Tag1 Consulting, Inc.)
  • godotislate

Collaboration

The design took years to settle because of a real safety concern: alexpott identified in comment #46 that reading config during import can require autoloading code for a module that isn't installed yet, which risks crashing on missing classes. neclimdul (#78) and phenaproxima (#84) pushed back hard, worried that letting config schema influence what gets autoloaded was a "danger zone" that could snowball to cover removed modules, themes and profiles too. alexpott resolved the disagreement by scoping AutoloadingStorage narrowly: it only wraps the sync storage (never active storage) and only for extensions genuinely being installed, and argued failures in this area should fail loudly rather than be silently tolerated. Wim Leers separately pushed for decoding !php/enum (not just !php/const) to match Symfony's own documented behavior and keep the PECL and Symfony YAML backends consistent, which alexpott agreed to add. Late in the process mondrake decided that supporting global constants declared in procedural .module files, a gap mikelutz had surfaced with a failing test, wasn't worth the added complexity and dropped it before the final commit.

item.title: #3588379: Move search from user module to Search
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 24 files, +345/−120 · php +332/−114 · yml +12/−5 · twig +1/−1
  • Diff: dc2a1d8
  • Discussion: #3588379 · 6 contributors · 34 comments
  • Followers: 7

Summary

The "Users" search plugin, previously bundled inside the User module, has been moved into a new core submodule called Search user, following the same pattern already used to split search functionality out of the Node and Help modules. Existing sites are upgraded automatically: a database update enables the new search_user module whenever user is already installed, and the user_search search page configuration now depends on search_user instead of user. No end user visible change is expected; the Users search page and its results work the same as before.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • Deprecation: Drupal\user\Plugin\Search\UserSearch is deprecated in favor of Drupal\search_user\Plugin\Search\SearchUser in the new search_user module; the old plugin now returns no results and denies access.

Technical details

The old Drupal\user\Plugin\Search\UserSearch plugin in user.module is now @deprecated (removed in Drupal 12.0.0, see the linked change record) and its execute() and access() methods are stubbed out to return no results and deny access respectively; the real implementation moved verbatim to Drupal\search_user\Plugin\Search\SearchUser in the new search_user module.

Unlike the earlier node and help extractions, search_user sorts alphabetically before user, so normal module-precedence rules would let the old, now-inert UserSearch plugin win when both modules are enabled. To avoid that, search_user implements hook_search_plugin_alter() (SearchUserHooks::searchPluginAlter()) to force the user_search plugin definition's class to the new SearchUser regardless of load order. A new search_update_11403() installs search_user automatically for any site that has user enabled but not yet search_user, and search.schema.yml's search.plugin.user_search config schema moved from user.module to the new module. search.module's help text was also hardened with a try/catch around Url::fromRoute('search.view'), since that route only exists once a default search page is configured, which was surfacing as a fatal error in the generic module test.

Upgrade

Update references to the deprecated plugin class:

// Before
use Drupal\user\Plugin\Search\UserSearch;

// After
use Drupal\search_user\Plugin\Search\SearchUser;

Contrib modules and custom code that enable Search functionality for users should depend on search_user (not just user), and any .info.yml or test $modules list that expects the user_search search page to work must include search_user.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: May 5, 2026
  • Committed: July 26, 2026 (2 months later)

Collaboration

Catch flagged a design issue partway through review: because search_user sorts alphabetically before user (unlike the node/help precedents, where the new module came later), the deprecated plugin would otherwise win by module precedence. That observation led to adding hook_search_plugin_alter() in search_user to force the correct plugin class, which quietone and dcam then verified worked via manual before/after upgrade testing.

item.title: #3579778: Removed modules should be included as a replace in composer.json
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Major task
  • Version: 10.6.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 2 files, +5/−1 · json +4 · lock +1/−1
  • Diff: 9a68ba6
  • Discussion: #3579778 · 12 contributors · 54 comments
  • Followers: 21

Summary

Several modules that used to live only in Drupal core (Ban, Contact, Field Layout, History, Search, Settings Tray, Shortcut, Stable9, Telephone, Toolbar) have been split out, or are being prepared to split out, into standalone contrib projects with their own drupal/<module> Composer package. Because core's composer.json did not declare these as "replaced" packages, Composer could get confused when a site or another dependency (as reported for the Forum, Pathauto and Metatag modules depending on History) required the new standalone release: it would try to resolve both the core-bundled code and the contrib package under the same name, producing conflicts. This change adds the appropriate entries to core's composer.json replace section so Composer knows the bundled core version already satisfies that package name, avoiding the conflict for site owners who add these contrib releases as dependencies.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Config change: Core's composer.json replace section now lists formerly core-only modules that have separate contrib releases (varies by branch), telling Composer that installing drupal/core-recommended/core already satisfies that package name.

Technical details

Core's composer.json replace array previously contained only Symfony polyfill entries; a general module replace mechanism had been removed from core in #3292380. This issue restores targeted entries, but with different lists per branch because of version-specific risk: on 10.6.x, the replace list gained drupal/ban, drupal/contact, drupal/field_layout, drupal/history, drupal/search, drupal/settings_tray, drupal/shortcut, drupal/stable9, drupal/telephone and drupal/toolbar, all modules already deprecated in Drupal 10 with stable contrib releases. On 11.x (main/12.0-dev) and 11.4.x, only drupal/search, drupal/settings_tray, drupal/shortcut and drupal/toolbar were added: modules that don't yet have a contrib release. Ban, Contact, Field Layout, History, Stable9 and Telephone were deliberately left out of the 11.x/11.4.x replace list because sites on those branches may already be requiring the contrib releases directly (see #3482198 for Ban's deprecation), and adding a core-side replace there would force Composer to fall back to the bundled core version instead of the contrib package a site had intentionally installed. composer.lock's content-hash was regenerated in each commit to match.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: March 17, 2026
  • Committed: July 25, 2026 (4 months and 3 commits later)

Key contributors

  • pcambra (Cambrico)
  • quietone (PreviousNext)
  • berdir (MD Systems GmbH)
  • cmlara (DM13 Security LLC)
  • dcam
  • smustgrave (Mobomo)
  • catch (Tag1 Consulting, Inc.)
  • godotislate

Collaboration

berdir reported that the missing replace entry for History was breaking downstream testing of the Forum module (and in turn Pathauto and Metatag), pushing this from a theoretical concern to an active breakage affecting the 11.2 branch as well. catch worked out the phased branch strategy: since a site on 11.3+ could already be using the contrib releases of Contact, Ban, Field Layout or History directly, adding those to the 11.x/11.4.x replace list would wrongly force Composer back to the bundled core version, so only modules without existing contrib releases (Search, Settings Tray, Shortcut, Toolbar) were added there, while 10.6.x got the full list. cmlara additionally argued for reconsidering the earlier removal of core's replace mechanism (#3292380) and filed #3582324 to think about the underlying Composer facade for future major versions. smustgrave did the legwork of opening the separate merge requests for the 11.x, 11.4.x and 10.6.x branches, and godotislate committed the changes, dropping some unrelated "allowed plugins" entries from the 10.6.x branch after review and waiting for catch's confirmation before committing that branch.

item.title: #3611847: Deprecate unused PdoTrait code
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 1 file, +28/−0 · php +28
  • Diff: ed2f681
  • Discussion: #3611847 · 4 contributors · 21 comments
  • Followers: 5

Summary

Several protected helper methods and a property in Drupal core's PdoTrait (used by PDO-based database drivers) were found to be dead code, no longer called anywhere in core. They are now formally deprecated and will be removed in Drupal 13. There is no replacement, since nothing in core needs them anymore. Sites and modules are unaffected unless they maintain a custom database driver that extends or calls into these internals.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • Deprecation: PdoTrait::$fetchModeLiterals, pdoToFetchAs(), clientFetchColumn(), clientFetchObject(), and clientQueryString() are deprecated for removal in Drupal 13, with no replacement.

Technical details

pdoToFetchAs() became unused once #3522561 fully typed StatementInterface method parameters, removing the need to convert legacy \PDO::FETCH_* integer constants to the FetchAs enum at that call site. clientFetchColumn(), clientFetchObject(), and clientQueryString() were likewise found to have no remaining callers in core. Each now carries an @deprecated in drupal:11.5.0 and is removed from drupal:13.0.0 docblock and, for the three methods, an @trigger_error() call emitting an E_USER_DEPRECATED notice pointing to the change record at drupal.org/node/3611848.

The protected array $fetchModeLiterals property (used only for building deprecation/error messages, mapping \PDO::FETCH_* constants to their literal names) is deprecated too. As discussed in the issue thread, this property had been moved from FetchModeTrait into PdoTrait five months earlier in #3525077, so the deprecation was applied at its current location in PdoTrait.

Upgrade

Custom database drivers or contrib code that override or call PdoTrait::pdoToFetchAs(), clientFetchColumn(), clientFetchObject(), clientQueryString(), or read PdoTrait::$fetchModeLiterals should remove that usage before Drupal 13, since there is no replacement:

// Deprecated, will be removed in Drupal 13 with no replacement:
protected function pdoToFetchAs(int $mode): FetchAs { ... }
protected function clientFetchColumn(int $column = 0): int|float|string|bool|NULL { ... }
protected function clientFetchObject(?string $class = NULL, array $constructorArguments = []): object|FALSE { ... }
protected function clientQueryString(): string { ... }

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: July 19, 2026
  • First commit: July 22, 2026 (3 days later)
  • Last commit: July 25, 2026 (2 days and 2 commits later)

Key contributors

  • mondrake
  • danielveza (PreviousNext)
  • dcam
  • catch (Tag1 Consulting, Inc.)

item.title: #3612963: Drop older dependency versions in Drupal 12
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: main
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 6 files, +18/−18 · json +10/−10 · lock +8/−8
  • Diff: 87de709
  • Discussion: #3612963 · 3 contributors · 10 comments
  • Followers: 5

Summary

For Drupal 12, core's composer.json now pins several third-party PHP dependencies to a single, newer major version instead of allowing a range spanning older and newer majors. This tidies up the dependency graph now that Drupal 12 no longer needs to support the older majors for backward compatibility, but it means any site or contributed project that still requires the older major version of one of these libraries will need to update before it can run on Drupal 12.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Requirements: Drupal 12 core now requires guzzlehttp/guzzle ^8.0 (dropping ^7.10), guzzlehttp/psr7 ^3.0 (dropping ^2.8), doctrine/lexer ^3 (dropping ^2), egulias/email-validator ^4.0 (dropping ^3.2.1), sebastian/diff ^7 (dropping ^4/^5/^6), and justinrainbow/json-schema ^6.5.2 (dropping ^5.2).

Technical details

The change is confined to composer.json (and the corresponding composer.lock/composer.json in core). Constraints were narrowed from dual-major ranges to single majors: doctrine/lexer from ^2 || ^3 to ^3, guzzlehttp/guzzle from ^7.10 || ^8.0 to ^8.0, guzzlehttp/psr7 from ^2.8.0 || ^3.0 to ^3.0, egulias/email-validator from ^3.2.1|^4.0 to ^4.0, sebastian/diff from ^4 || ^5 || ^6 || ^7 to ^7, and justinrainbow/json-schema from ^5.2 || ^6.5.2 to ^6.5.2. The dev-only micheh/phpcs-gitlab requirement was similarly narrowed from ^1.1 || ^2.0 to ^2.0.

The motivation, per the issue, was that #3612544 added Guzzle 8 support while still nominally allowing Guzzle 7, but it wasn't clear the code actually supported both. Rather than audit for true dual-version compatibility, this issue takes the opportunity of the Drupal 12 major release to require a clean, single version of each of these libraries going forward.</technical> <parameter name="upgrade">Sites and contributed projects targeting Drupal 12 must ensure their composer.json allows the newer major versions of these libraries:

"doctrine/lexer": "^3",
"guzzlehttp/guzzle": "^8.0",
"guzzlehttp/psr7": "^3.0",
"egulias/email-validator": "^4.0",
"sebastian/diff": "^7",
"justinrainbow/json-schema": "^6.5.2"

Code that relied on APIs only present in the dropped major versions (for example Guzzle 7) should be updated to the versions above.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: July 24, 2026
  • Committed: July 24, 2026

Key contributors

  • longwave (Full Fat Things)
  • larowlan (PreviousNext)

item.title: #3608184: Load multiple cardinality fields with a smaller result set
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Major task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 7 files, +191/−64 · php +191/−64
  • Diff: 35c7c09
  • Discussion: #3608184 · 7 contributors · 47 comments
  • Followers: 13

Summary

When an entity has several multi-value ("multiple cardinality") fields, Drupal core previously ran one query per field and then re-sorted the results in PHP. This change combines those queries into a single, more efficient query per chunk of fields, cutting down the number of database queries needed to load such entities. This is a purely internal performance optimization to entity loading. There is nothing for site owners or module developers to configure or change; Drupal's own performance tests recorded fewer queries on pages like the front page and node pages after this change.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

This is a follow-up to #3607938, which found that naively joining multiple multi-value field tables together in one query produces a cartesian product (a row for every combination of deltas across fields). This issue's fix, in SqlContentEntityStorage::loadMultipleCardinalityFields(), avoids that by building a "delta spine": a subselect that UNIONs the (entity_id, langcode, delta) rows from each dedicated field table in the chunk, giving the full set of valid delta combinations for the loaded entities. Each field's dedicated table is then LEFT JOINed onto that spine (aliased delta_join) matching on ID, langcode and delta, so every field's value lines up on the correct row without multiplying against other fields. When a chunk contains only one multiple-cardinality field, the union step is skipped entirely and the query selects straight from that field's table, since a single table can't multiply against itself.

loadFromDedicatedTables() now chunks the multiple-cardinality fields together (via array_chunk() using the same FIELD_MINIMUM_CHUNK_SIZE used for single-cardinality fields) and calls loadMultipleCardinalityFields() once per chunk instead of once per field, and the previous PHP-side ksort() re-sort of deltas is removed since the query now does ORDER BY on the delta from the spine. The method signature was reworked accordingly: the $base_query, $base_table, $base_id_key, and $base_langcode_alias parameters were dropped since the query is now built independently of the base entity query, and an $ids parameter was added to constrain the spine and field tables directly. EXPLAIN output shared in the issue confirmed the union/join query hits indexes on every branch, and Drupal's PerformanceTest suites were updated to reflect the reduced query counts (for example the Umami front page cold cache dropped from 184 to 178 queries, and the standard profile node page cold cache dropped from 204 to 195).

catch explored several alternatives before landing on this approach: a new database table pre-populated with sequential delta values to join against (rejected as "a bit painful" and hard to size for sites with very high cardinality), and separately ruled out UNION of the actual field data (column type mismatches), a temporary table, a MySQL sequence, and GROUP BY (no reliable delta to group on), documenting why each wouldn't work. alexpott then proposed building the delta spine from a UNION subselect of just the (id, langcode, delta) tuples instead of a physical table, and further simplified it to drop the join to the base entity table entirely. catch called this approach avoiding "the crime against databases" of the earlier table-based idea and moved the issue to RTBC. item.title: #3569316: Client connection ($clientConnection) must be of type object, null given when deleting a node
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Major bug report
  • Version: 11.4.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 2 files, +34/−0 · php +34
  • Diff: 478fb37
  • Discussion: #3569316 · 14 contributors · 41 comments
  • Followers: 24

Summary

A fatal TypeError could occur during common content operations (saving or deleting nodes, flushing caches, language switches) on Drupal 11.3+, causing the cachetags table to not be updated and leaving caches permanently stale until manually rebuilt. The error was intermittent but reliably reproducible on PHP 8.4 and in multi-replica PHP-FPM setups. This fix ensures cache tag invalidation and all other post-transaction callbacks complete correctly on every request.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

PHP's object destruction order during request shutdown is undefined. If Connection::__destruct() executed before Transaction::__destruct(), the Connection would set its internal $this->connection PDO property to NULL. When Transaction::__destruct() subsequently ran purge() → processPostTransactionCallbacks(), any registered callback that used the database (such as DatabaseCacheTagsChecksum::rootTransactionEndCallback → doInvalidateTags()) would call Connection::prepareStatement() with a null PDO, throwing StatementWrapperIterator::__construct(): Argument #2 ($clientConnection) must be of type object, null given.

The fix adds a $this->processPostTransactionCallbacks() call at the end of TransactionManagerBase::commitAll(). commitAll() is already invoked during PHP shutdown via commitAllOnShutdown to unwind any open transaction stack. By also draining the post-transaction callback queue there, all callbacks execute while the Connection object is still fully initialized, before any destructors can run. The same pattern applies to any module that registers its own callbacks via TransactionManagerInterface::addPostTransactionCallback().

A new kernel test testPostTransactionsAlwaysExecutedBeforeConnectionIsDestroyed in TransactionTest verifies the scenario: it closes the connection and unsets the transaction in the same destructor-race order, then confirms the callback's side-effects are present after reopening the connection. A one-line PHPStan suppression comment (// @phpstan-ignore unset.possiblyHookedProperty) was removed from the test file in the 11.x and 11.4.x follow-up commits to pass static analysis. The related cleanup issue #3406985 (converting core transactions to explicit commitOrRelease()) was a related but separate effort and did not fix this callback-ordering problem.

item.title: #3612544: Update to Guzzle 8
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Critical task
  • Version: main
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 13 files, +78/−307 · lock +42/−257 · php +34/−42 · json +2/−8

  • Discussion: #3612544 · 4 contributors · 16 comments

Summary

Drupal core now ships with Guzzle 8.0, upgraded from 7.x. The composer.json constraint is broadened to ^7.10 || ^8.0 (and guzzlehttp/psr7 to ^2.8.0 || ^3.0), so sites can still resolve Guzzle 7 when other dependencies force it. The installed lock file pins guzzlehttp/guzzle 8.0.0, guzzlehttp/psr7 3.0.0, and guzzlehttp/promises 3.0.0. The dev dependency php-http/guzzle7-adapter is removed because no Guzzle 8 compatible release exists for it.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Requirements: Guzzle 8.0.0, guzzlehttp/psr7 3.0.0, and guzzlehttp/promises 3.0.0 are now locked; core composer.json allows ^7.10 || ^8.0 for guzzle and ^2.8.0 || ^3.0 for psr7.

Technical details

The composer.json version constraints for guzzlehttp/guzzle and guzzlehttp/psr7 are widened to accept both major versions. ralouphie/getallheaders drops out of the lock file because guzzlehttp/psr7 3.x no longer depends on it.

Guzzle 8 removes ClientInterface::getConfig() entirely, so three PHPStan $ignoreErrors entries suppressing that deprecation warning (in BrowserTestBase, ClientFactoryTest, and DrupalTestBrowser) are deleted. In DrupalTestBrowser::doRequest(), the catch block previously caught RequestException and had to guard against a null response; Guzzle 8's BadResponseException (covering 4xx and 5xx responses) always carries a response, so the null-response branch and the old RequestException import are removed.

Guzzle 8 requires handler callables to return a PromiseInterface rather than a ResponseInterface directly. A mock handler in LocaleTranslationTest is updated to wrap its Response in Create::promiseFor() and declare the correct return type signature function(RequestInterface $request, array $options): PromiseInterface.

Guzzle 8's CookieJar no longer stores a Secure-flagged cookie received over a non-HTTPS connection (the HTTPS mock used in browser tests is not a real TLS connection). LoginHttpsTest::loginHttps() is updated to parse the Set-Cookie response header directly with SetCookie::fromString() instead of calling CookieJar::getCookieByName(). A companion fix in BrowserTestBase::getSessionCookies() guards against a null session ID before building the cookie jar.

Guzzle 8 also trims the trailing newline that earlier versions appended to the response body excerpt in exception messages, so several test string assertions drop the trailing \n.

Upgrade

Custom Guzzle handlers must return a PromiseInterface instead of a ResponseInterface:

// Before (Guzzle 7)
$handler = function (RequestInterface $request, array $options): ResponseInterface {
    return new Response(200, [], 'body');
};

// After (Guzzle 8)
use GuzzleHttp\Promise\Create;
use GuzzleHttp\Promise\PromiseInterface;

$handler = function (RequestInterface $request, array $options): PromiseInterface {
    return Create::promiseFor(new Response(200, [], 'body'));
};

Exception handling for 4xx/5xx responses should use BadResponseException instead of RequestException:

// Before (Guzzle 7)
use GuzzleHttp\Exception\RequestException;
catch (RequestException $e) {
    if (!$e->hasResponse()) {
        throw $e;
    }
    $response = $e->getResponse();
}

// After (Guzzle 8)
use GuzzleHttp\Exception\BadResponseException;
catch (BadResponseException $e) {
    $response = $e->getResponse();
}

Remove any calls to getConfig() on GuzzleHttp\Client or GuzzleHttp\ClientInterface; that method is removed in Guzzle 8. Store configuration values your code needs at construction time instead of reading them back from the client.

Summary

BatchStorageInterface now declares a getId(): int method. Previously the method existed only on the concrete BatchStorage class, yet Drupal core called it through the interface type-hint, creating a contract gap. Any module that provides a custom implementation of BatchStorageInterface must now add this method.

Affects module maintainers.

The ProxyClass\Batch\BatchStorage generated proxy already declared getId(): int, so no changes to that class were needed.

If you have a custom class that implements BatchStorageInterface, add the getId() method:

 * {@inheritdoc}

    // Your implementation here.

Summary

Install profiles can now list recipes in their .info.yml file under a recipes key, and Drupal will apply those recipes automatically as part of the installation batch, immediately after modules are installed. Previously, a profile that wanted to apply a recipe had to use workarounds like Drupal CMS does. This change eliminates that need and lets profiles combine traditional module installation with recipe-based configuration in a single, declarative step.

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Config change: Profile .info.yml files gain an optional recipes list key recognized by install_profile_modules().
  • New API: New recipes key supported in install profile .info.yml files; lists recipe directory paths to apply during installation.

Technical details

The change is a small addition to install_profile_modules() in the installer. After the module-install batch is assembled, the function reads $install_state['profile_info']['recipes'] and maps each path to a Recipe object using Recipe::createFromDirectory(...). It then calls RecipeRunner::toBatchOperations() on each recipe and appends the resulting operations to the same BatchBuilder, so recipes run in the order listed, back-to-back with module installs.

Path resolution follows the existing convention: core recipe paths (e.g. core/recipes/audio_media_type) work as-is because RecipeConfigurator already has special handling for the core/ prefix. Paths to contributed recipes require the caller to provide a fully-resolvable directory path; a dedicated follow-up (#3612240) will address resolving contributed recipe paths via Composer configuration. Recipe translation during install (downloading .po files before applying) is also deferred to a separate issue.

To use this feature in a custom install profile, add a recipes key to the profile's .info.yml:

name: My Profile
type: profile
install:
  - some_module
recipes:
  - core/recipes/audio_media_type

Recipes are applied in the listed order after module installation completes. Core recipe paths (prefixed with core/) resolve out of the box. Contributed recipe paths must currently be absolute or relative to the web root; a path-resolution follow-up is tracked in #3612240.

item.title: #3101714: Link field display should show plaintext URLs longer than 80 chars
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core

Summary

Link fields configured to display URLs as plain text (the "URL only" or "Show URL as plain text" formatter options) no longer truncate the URL at 80 characters. Previously, the default 80-character trim was applied regardless of display mode, which silently produced broken URLs whenever a URL exceeded that length and had no separate title. The trim remains active for standard hyperlinked display, where truncating the visible text does not break the underlying link. This change affects both new and existing link fields at render time.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Config change: Existing link fields with url_only or url_plain enabled and a non-zero trim_length will now render full URLs at display time, regardless of the stored trim_length value.

In LinkFormatter::viewElements(), the call to Unicode::truncate() was previously guarded only by !empty($settings['trim_length']). The condition is now !empty($settings['trim_length']) && empty($settings['url_plain']) && empty($settings['url_only']), so trimming fires only when the link is rendered as a standard anchor tag. The same guard was added to settingsSummary(), so the "Link text trimmed to N characters" message is also suppressed when it would be inaccurate. In the formatter settings form, the trim_length element gains a #states rule that hides it in the UI when url_only is checked. The default value of trim_length (80) is unchanged in defaultSettings(); what changed is whether that value is honored at render time. Tests in LinkFormatterDisplayTest and LinkSeparateFormatterDisplayTest add two new input fixtures: a URL longer than 80 characters with an explicit title, and the same URL with no title. Expected results confirm that plain-text and URL-only display modes now render the full URL while anchor-tag display still applies the trim.

As part of the change, approximately 176 existing core Twig files were reformatted to comply with the new rules. Developers contributing Twig templates to core (or wanting to follow core conventions in contrib or custom themes) now have an official tool and a reference configuration to work from. Site owners are not affected; the reformatted templates produce identical rendered output.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: New Composer scripts composer twigcs and composer twigcs-fix for checking and auto-fixing Twig coding standard violations.

Technical details

The new core/.twig-cs-fixer.php configuration file registers Drupal's TwigTransTokenParser so the linter understands the {% trans %} tag, excludes tests/ directories from linting, and applies the TwigCsFixer standard (which implements the official Twig coding standards at twig.symfony.com). Two rules are overridden for Drupal: IndentRule(spaceRatio: 2) for 2-space indentation and CompactHashRule(TRUE) to require no spaces around inline hash literals (e.g. {key: value} rather than { 'key': value }). allowNonFixableRules() is called so the config works in both lint and fix modes.

Two Composer scripts are added: composer twigcs runs a lint check and composer twigcs-fix auto-fixes violations. A new 🧹 Twig Coding standards (twig-cs-fixer) job is added to the GitLab CI Lint stage; on merge-request pipelines it only triggers when .twig files, core/.twig-cs-fixer.php, or composer.json/composer.lock change. Cache artifacts use the file core/.twigcsfixercache, which is added to .gitignore and wired into the existing CI cache download/upload pattern alongside the PHP and JS caches. The commit-code-check.sh pre-commit script is also updated to run the linter against any staged .twig files, and to re-lint all files when the config itself changes.

The bulk reformatting of the ~176 existing core files normalized four categories of style: {% include 'tmpl' %} tags became {{ include('tmpl') }} function calls; {% include 'tmpl' with {...} only %} became {{ include('tmpl', {...}, with_context: false) }}; double-quoted string literals became single-quoted; and hash array keys were converted from quoted form ({'key': value}) to unquoted form ({key: value}) where the key is a valid identifier. Trailing commas were also added to multi-line array and argument lists.

Upgrade

No changes are required for existing sites. Developers contributing Twig templates to Drupal core can check their files with:

composer twigcs

And auto-fix violations with:

composer twigcs-fix

The configuration lives in core/.twig-cs-fixer.php. Custom modules or themes that want to adopt the same standards can reference that file as a starting point, though the TwigTransTokenParser registration it contains is only needed when linting templates that use Drupal's {% trans %} tag.

item.title: #3485030: Avoid saving menu links through node form when they do not change
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 2 files, +43/−2 · php +43/−2
  • Diff: c4d7966
  • Discussion: #3485030 · 11 contributors · 48 comments
  • Followers: 22

Summary

When an editor saves a node through the node edit form without making any changes to the associated menu link, Drupal previously saved the menu_link_content entity unconditionally, triggering postSave() and invalidating the config:system.menu.MENUNAME cache tag every time. Because menus are rendered on most pages, this caused broad, unnecessary cache invalidation across CDNs and page caches. After this fix, the menu link entity is only saved when something actually changed, preventing spurious invalidation of menu cache tags on unrelated node saves.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The fix is in MenuUiHelper::menuUiNodeSave() in menu_ui. Previously, $entity->save() was called unconditionally at the end of the function regardless of whether any menu link fields had changed. The fix splits that single save call into two paths. For the branch that handles updating an existing menu_link_content entity (when $values['entity_id'] is set), $entity->setOriginal(clone $entity) is called immediately after loading, which arms the entity's change tracking. For the else branch (pending-revision handling), a $default_revision_change flag is computed by comparing $entity->isDefaultRevision() with $node->isDefaultRevision(), and $entity->save() is now gated on $default_revision_change || $entity->hasTranslationChanges(). Using hasTranslationChanges() alone was not sufficient because it does not detect a default-to-non-default revision transition; that required the explicit separate flag. An earlier approach proposed implementing the skip logic inside MenuTreeStorage::doSave(), but that was rejected because the storage layer is not declared internal and because MenuLinkContent::postSave() writes only the active-language title into the tree storage, making a purely storage-level comparison unreliable for multilingual sites (see comment #26). The new test coverage in MenuNodeFormWidgetTest verifies the cache_tags.invalidator.checksum service before and after various scenarios: no-op saves do not increment the checksum; adding, modifying weight, and deleting a menu link do. The fix also uncovered a separate bug in how content moderation and non-default revisions interacted, which was resolved as a prerequisite in #3499181.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: November 1, 2024
  • Committed: July 20, 2026 (1 year and 2 commits later)

Key contributors

  • achap
  • kristiaanvandeneynde (Factorial.io)
  • berdir (MD Systems GmbH)
  • andy_w (Numiko)
  • nicxvan (nLightened Development LLC)
  • dcam
  • catch (Tag1 Consulting, Inc.)

Collaboration

berdir drove the final implementation after the original approach (changing MenuTreeStorage::doSave() return value, proposed by achap) was found to be a risky behavior change for multilingual sites. In comment #26, berdir explained that MenuLinkContent::postSave() only writes the active-language title into the tree storage, so any storage-level equality check would silently drop multilingual data. berdir opened a new MR targeting menu_ui instead, then hit a test failure tracing back to a content-moderation bug introduced years earlier (credited partly to berdir's own past work) that allowed saving a default revision as a non-default revision. That was spun out and fixed as a prerequisite in #3499181. After that blocker landed, berdir switched the change-detection logic from explicit field comparisons to hasTranslationChanges(), then discovered that method misses the default-revision flag, requiring the explicit $default_revision_change guard. achap closed the original MR once the community agreed the storage-layer approach was not safe.

item.title: #3595652: Deprecate module.inc contents
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 21 files, +158/−112 · php +155/−111 · yml +3/−1
  • Diff: daf0e8e
  • Discussion: #3595652 · 6 contributors · 27 comments
  • Followers: 8

Summary

The two procedural functions in module.inc that manage module weights, module_set_weight() and module_config_sort(), are deprecated in Drupal 11.5.0 and will be removed in Drupal 13.0.0. Their logic has been moved into a new Drupal\Core\Extension\ModuleWeight service, which provides equivalent set() and sort() methods. Modules that call either procedural function directly need to switch to the service before upgrading to Drupal 13.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: ModuleInstaller::__construct() gained a new nullable ?ModuleWeight $moduleWeight parameter; it will be required in drupal:12.0.0.
  • Deprecation: module_set_weight() and module_config_sort() in module.inc deprecated in drupal:11.5.0 and removed in drupal:13.0.0; replaced by Drupal\Core\Extension\ModuleWeight::set() and ::sort().
  • New API: New Drupal\Core\Extension\ModuleWeight service with set(string $module, int $weight): void and sort(array $data): array methods.

Technical details

The new Drupal\Core\Extension\ModuleWeight class lives in core/lib/Drupal/Core/Extension/ModuleWeight.php and is registered as an autowired service. It accepts ModuleHandlerInterface and ConfigFactoryInterface via constructor injection. ModuleWeight::set(string $module, int $weight): void replicates the logic previously in module_set_weight(), including writing to core.extension config and updating the live module list in the module handler. ModuleWeight::sort(array $data): array replicates the sign-prefix plus zero-padded integer plus name string-sort algorithm from module_config_sort().

The procedural functions in module.inc now contain only a @trigger_error deprecation notice followed by a delegation call to \Drupal::service(ModuleWeight::class). All internal callers across Drupal core (including ModuleInstaller, ExcludedModulesEventSubscriber, the installer's install_finished(), content_translation.install, views.install, and several test classes) have been updated to use the service directly.

ModuleInstaller::__construct() gained a new nullable ?ModuleWeight $moduleWeight parameter at the end of its signature; a deprecation notice is triggered if the argument is absent when the class is constructed, and the argument will be required in Drupal 12.0.0. ExcludedModulesEventSubscriber similarly gained ModuleWeight as a new constructor argument and its service definition in core.services.yml was updated accordingly.

Upgrade

Replace calls to module_set_weight() with the ModuleWeight service:

// Before (deprecated since 11.5.0):
module_set_weight('mymodule', 10);

// After:
use Drupal\Core\Extension\ModuleWeight;
\Drupal::service(ModuleWeight::class)->set('mymodule', 10);

Replace calls to module_config_sort() with the ModuleWeight service:

// Before (deprecated since 11.5.0):
$sorted = module_config_sort($modules);

// After:
use Drupal\Core\Extension\ModuleWeight;
$sorted = \Drupal::service(ModuleWeight::class)->sort($modules);

If you extend or directly instantiate ModuleInstaller, add ModuleWeight as the final constructor argument. See the change record at https://www.drupal.org/node/3595653.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: June 11, 2026
  • First commit: July 14, 2026 (1 month later)
  • Last commit: July 20, 2026 (5 days and 2 commits later)

item.title: #3588274: Remove Tags vocabulary from Standard profile and recipe
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 4 files, +0/−16 · yml +0/−15 · php +0/−1
  • Diff: 0654319
  • Discussion: #3588274 · 6 contributors · 26 comments
  • Followers: 8

Summary

New Drupal installations using the Standard profile or the standard recipe no longer include a "Tags" taxonomy vocabulary. The content_editor role also no longer receives the create terms in tags and edit terms in tags permissions. Sites that need a Tags vocabulary must now create one manually after installation. This is part of a broader effort to pare down the Standard profile to a minimal baseline, following the earlier removal of the Article and Basic page content types (#3587118) and the Comment module dependency (#3588276).

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Config change: The taxonomy.vocabulary.tags config object and the create terms in tags / edit terms in tags permissions on content_editor are no longer included in the Standard profile or standard recipe.

Technical details

The change deletes taxonomy.vocabulary.tags.yml from the standard recipe config directory. The content_editor role config (content_editor.yml) is updated to drop its dependency on both taxonomy.vocabulary.tags config and the taxonomy module itself, and to remove the create terms in tags and edit terms in tags permissions. The same permission removals are mirrored in the standard recipe's own role config snapshot. The StandardTest functional test is updated to remove taxonomy.vocabulary.tags from the expected list of installed config objects. The change was motivated by the fact that after the removal of the Article content type (which previously used the Tags field), the vocabulary was left floating with nothing referencing it.

Upgrade

If your site's deployment scripts, migration code, or tests assume the tags vocabulary exists in a fresh Standard install, you must either create the vocabulary explicitly or add it via a custom recipe/install hook. The content_editor role will also no longer have taxonomy term permissions, so any code granting that role and expecting tag editing rights must be updated.
